1.why: All seven screens are static, flat panels with no carousels, banners, animations or modal pop-ups; only inline status messages appear.

2.why: Headings, the highlighted current progress step and the single filled primary button (e.g. 'Send recovery code', 'Verify code', 'Accept updated privacy conditions') stand out clearly, though the dark activity log block competes visually for attention.

3.why: Each page has one main task, one input field and one primary action plus a persistent progress list, making the next thing to do easy to locate; the extra security notes and log panel add a little scanning effort.

4.why: The step list, 'Step X of 6' labels, on-page password checklist and inline next-step prompts mean little must be held in memory, though the recovery/MFA codes still have to be carried from the log/delivery message to the input field.

5.why: No 'remember me' checkbox, autofill hint, password-manager suggestion or show-password toggle appears on any screen, including the sign-in and create-password steps.

6.why: Only the synthetic demo email is displayed as a hint on step 1; there are no saved accounts, remembered devices or recognisable stored items presented to the user.

7.why: Sentences are short, plain and consistently phrased (e.g. 'Step 3 of 6. Choose a new password. We will not show or log it.'), though several security/session notes such as 'This replacement approval is short-lived and single-use' are jargon-heavy.

8.why: No error state is shown in any of the seven screenshots, so the presence of problem-plus-fix error messaging cannot be evidenced; only success confirmations are visible.

9.why: Step 1 gives a concrete email example and step 3 lists an explicit password checklist, but the recovery and security code fields show no example format or length hint.

10.why: The choices offered (send recovery code vs. 'I know my password — sign in', simulated delivery link vs. manual code box) are clearly labelled, but only password and one-time code methods exist — no biometric/face option is presented.

11.why: Each screen presents one primary action with at most two or three secondary options (pause, resume, back, help), keeping the choice load low.

12.why: Every step displays an explicit outcome banner, e.g. 'New password saved securely. Next, confirm your security code.' and 'Security code confirmed. You are signed in.'

13.why: A persistent 'Help and safe sign-in' panel with a 'Show a short reminder' button and per-step guidance lines ('Next: open the simulated delivery message...') is on every screen.

14.why: 'Back to recovery request', 'Resume recovery' and 'Return to secure start' allow retrying, and codes can be re-entered, but no visible retry-after-error message or 'resend code' control is shown.

15.why: All seven screens reuse the identical layout: header banner, left progress column with the same pause/resume buttons, centred titled card, and bottom help and activity-log blocks.
